binders: A real number t is universally quantified.
conclusions: The real-valued mass of the closed upper ray [t, infinity) under gaussianReal 0 1 is at most exp(-t^2/2)/sqrt(2*pi).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 is gaussianReal 0 1, the real Gaussian measure with location parameter 0 and nonnegative parameter 1.
Set.Ici t is the closed upper ray [t, infinity).
For a measure mu and set A, Measure.real mu A is the real conversion of the extended-nonnegative value mu(A).
The right-hand side is (1/sqrt(2*pi)) * exp(-t^2/2), the usual Gaussian density expression at t.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real t at least 1, the mass assigned by the Gaussian measure gaussianReal 0 1 to the closed upper tail [t, infinity) is at most the Gaussian density factor exp(-t^2/2)/sqrt(2*pi).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: No assertion is made for t < 1.
The set [t, infinity) includes its endpoint t.
The conclusion is a single non-strict upper bound; it contains no lower bound or equality.
The result concerns the real-converted mass of a fixed measure directly and does not quantify a random variable or probability space.
Measure.real would lose information at an infinite measure value because it uses ENNReal.toReal, but the supplied Gaussian-measure interpretation is intended to make this tail mass finite.
The right-hand side contains no factor 1/t.
The statement gives an exact inequality, not an asymptotic equivalence.
The hypothesis t >= 1 makes t positive, but the target itself does not divide by t.
ambiguities: The one-level definition of gaussianReal refers to gaussianPDF without expanding that density, so the packet does not independently expose its normalization formula or prove that gaussianReal 0 1 has finite total mass.

The supplied dependency boundary identifies the second gaussianReal parameter only as an NNReal and shows how it selects the Dirac versus density branch; its statistical interpretation is not further expanded in the packet.
